metadata.audience: English-speaking independent visitors interested in heritage, mountain walking, architecture or a carefully bounded beginner Tai Chi observation, 2–4 nights
metadata.promise: Read Wudang as a mountain-based Taoist architectural and historical system, with an itinerary that respects weather, stairs, etiquette and uncertainty—not as a guaranteed kung fu or spiritual-transformation experience.
metadata.commercial_boundary: Research and human-checked digital roadbook only. No booking, transport, tickets, lodging, guide, physical training, medical/wellness claim, religious access, bundled travel or third-party experience sale.

source_policy.rule: Opening hours, entry rules, weather, cable-car operation, routes, transport, religious-space rules and every instructor/provider are dynamic. Human verification must precede client-specific output.

sources.title: UNESCO: Ancient Building Complex in the Wudang Mountains

modules.name: Heritage system, not fantasy
modules.question: What connects mountain, architecture, Taoism and Ming-era state building?
modules.output_rule: Begin with public heritage interpretation; do not promise religious access.

modules.name: Arrival and protected pace
modules.question: How many nights and how much transfer/step capacity does this trip actually have?
modules.output_rule: No exact travel-time claim without current check.

modules.name: Mountain movement and weather
modules.question: What walking, stairs, cable-car and weather contingencies fit this visitor?

modules.name: Public architectural route
modules.question: Which public heritage layer is meaningful without overpacking the day?
modules.output_rule: Use a primary route and a fallback, never a static checklist.

modules.name: Religion, etiquette and photography
modules.question: How can a non-religious visitor engage respectfully?
modules.output_rule: Site rules and consent prevail; no ritual or sacred-access promise.

modules.name: Tai Chi / martial-arts boundary
modules.question: Is the person seeking observation, a beginner movement session, training or healing?
modules.output_rule: Only partner_ready providers may be named; no medical, lineage or authenticity claims.

modules.name: Accommodation, food and recovery
modules.question: Where should the traveller base themselves to protect rest, early starts and fallback capacity?
modules.output_rule: No hotel or restaurant ranking without date-specific human check.

modules.name: Roadbook release and escalation
modules.question: What needs a human check, and when should the agent stop?
modules.output_rule: Escalate health, mobility, weather, transport and all partner requests.

points.name: UNESCO heritage-system card
points.why_it_matters: The World Heritage property connects mountain landscapes with a long Taoist building tradition and surviving monumental architecture.
points.agent_use: Frame the visit as architecture, landscape and history together.

points.name: Ming state-building lens
points.why_it_matters: A stronger story than generic mysticism: imperial patronage, construction and religious legitimacy shaped the complex.
points.agent_use: Adjust historical depth to the visitor.

points.name: Public-vs-private access boundary
points.why_it_matters: Temples, practitioners and training spaces are not automatically tourism inventory.
points.agent_use: Never infer access from online marketing.

points.name: Two-night feasibility decision
points.why_it_matters: Two nights can support a focused heritage/mountain visit only if arrivals, weather and mobility remain workable.
points.agent_use: Do not add training or remote detours by default.

points.name: Three-to-four-night slow route decision
points.why_it_matters: Extra time creates a weather buffer and allows a separately vetted, low-intensity activity discussion.
points.agent_use: Still no partner recommendation without release.

points.name: Arrival and final-connection audit
points.why_it_matters: Last-mile arrival can decide whether a first day is usable or simply exhausting.
points.agent_use: Human-check date-specific connections.

points.name: Stairs and exertion disclosure
points.why_it_matters: Mountain routes can be stair-heavy and condition-sensitive; photos do not convey exertion.
points.agent_use: Ask mobility and exertion tolerance; no fitness assurance.

points.name: Rain, storm and cold fallback
points.why_it_matters: Weather may alter visibility, comfort and operations; it must change the day plan, not merely add a warning.
points.agent_use: Use official same-day information and a low-exposure fallback.

points.name: Cable-car operation boundary
points.why_it_matters: Operating status and queues are dynamic; static availability claims are unsafe.
points.agent_use: Ask client to verify official current status; never promise operation.

points.name: Primary public heritage route
points.why_it_matters: One coherent public route can connect building, slope and viewpoint without turning a mountain day into a race.
points.agent_use: Release only after operational field walk.

points.name: Low-exposure fallback route
points.why_it_matters: A useful roadbook needs a weather/energy fallback rather than a failed version of the main plan.
points.agent_use: Verify current accessible public areas.

points.name: Sunrise/photo expectation boundary
points.why_it_matters: Mist, sunrise, clear peaks and empty scenes cannot be sold as outcomes.
points.agent_use: Give decision conditions, never an image guarantee.

points.name: Temple etiquette card
points.why_it_matters: Respectful clothing, quiet behaviour, photography consent and local rules protect both visitors and worshippers.
points.agent_use: State that on-site rules supersede all guidance.

points.name: Non-religious visitor route
points.why_it_matters: Architecture and landscape can be meaningful without requiring participation in worship.
points.agent_use: Do not pressure participation or imply access.

points.name: Sacred/private-space refusal
points.why_it_matters: A request to meet a master, join ritual or enter non-public space has privacy and religious boundaries.
points.agent_use: Decline promise; collect research request only.

points.name: Beginner Tai Chi intent split
points.why_it_matters: Observation, a recreational session, serious training and healthcare are distinct needs.
points.agent_use: Ask goal, fitness and language before any resource discussion.

points.name: Tai Chi partner release gate
points.why_it_matters: Provider credentials, language, venue, emergency plan, capacity, waiver, pricing and cancellation evidence must exist.
points.agent_use: No name, quote, booking link or recommendation until partner_ready.

points.name: Training/healing refusal
points.why_it_matters: The roadbook is neither a martial-arts school broker nor healthcare service.
points.agent_use: State boundary and offer a research-only brief if appropriate.

points.name: Rest-and-base audit
points.why_it_matters: The right base depends on actual arrival, early start, sleep, recovery and weather fallback—not promotional hotel lists.
points.agent_use: Human-check current options and client needs.

points.name: Human-check release gate
points.why_it_matters: The safety and commercial quality of a roadbook depend on dated evidence, not confident prose.
points.agent_use: Do not label a product Human-checked unless audit records exist.

follow_up_questions.ask: Are you primarily here for public heritage/architecture, mountain walking, or an introduction to Taoist history?
Where do you arrive from, how many actual nights are protected, and can one day change for weather?
Are there mobility, stair, altitude, heart, injury or child-safety limits that require a human review?
Do you want observation, a recreational beginner session, or serious training? Which language and physical limits matter?
Are you asking for professional training or health support? Those are outside this roadbook and cannot be represented as a travel experience.
Would a respectful public heritage route meet your interest? Private religious access and ritual participation cannot be promised.
Can you accept a weather-dependent fallback and verify same-day official operating information?
Would you like a human-checked brief and official links while you make all bookings directly?

output_guardrails: Never promise a master, monk, temple residence, ritual participation, private space or religious outcome.
Never call a course authentic, official, medically beneficial, therapeutic or suitable for a particular condition.
Never promise weather, sunrise, mist, cable-car operation, open routes, crowds, tickets or transport.
Never give a high-exertion route to a visitor with disclosed health/mobility risk without human review.
Never name, price, book or promote a Tai Chi/martial provider before partner_ready evidence exists.
No booking, payment collection, guiding, packaged travel, ticket/transport/lodging sales or third-party experience sales.

launch_checks.name: Arrival and last-mile run
launch_checks.purpose: Actual transfer, station, payment, language and late-arrival friction.

launch_checks.name: Two-night field walk
launch_checks.purpose: Time, stairs, toilets, shelter, hydration, signal and exit points.

launch_checks.name: Weather/cable-car protocol
launch_checks.purpose: Official dynamic-information sources and fallback decisions.

launch_checks.name: Etiquette/photo rule audit
launch_checks.purpose: On-site public/private, photography and conduct rules.

launch_checks.name: Tai Chi provider release audit
launch_checks.purpose: Credentials, language, safety, waiver, consent, commercial evidence and trial feedback.

launch_checks.name: Accommodation/recovery audit
launch_checks.purpose: Base, rest, food, early-start and fallback feasibility.
